Native Getting Started with cpmr

Source: vignettes/native-getting-started.Rmd
native-getting-started.Rmd

Overview

cpmr’s primary workflow is a native, matrix-first API built around spec() together with cpm().

This vignette walks through:

  • how to shape CPM inputs;
  • how to run leakage-safe fold-based assessment;
  • how to inspect predictions and selected edges;
  • how custom resamples and missing-data handling work.

Prepare Inputs

CPM expects one row per subject and one column per edge.

  • conmat: an n x p connectivity matrix;
  • behav: a length-n numeric outcome vector;
  • covariates: an optional n x q nuisance matrix.
library(cpmr)

withr::local_seed(123)
n <- 80
p <- 200

conmat <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
covariates <- matrix(rnorm(n), ncol = 1)
behav <- rowMeans(conmat[, 1:12, drop = FALSE]) +
  0.5 * covariates[, 1] +
  rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)

Run CPM with cpm()

Use cpm() on a spec() object for an out-of-sample estimate of predictive performance.

result <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav,
  spec = spec(),
  covariates = covariates,
  resamples = 5
)

result
#> CPM:
#>   Call: cpm(conmat = conmat, behav = behav, spec = spec(), covariates = covariates, 
#>     resamples = 5)
#>   Number of folds: 5
#>   Number of observations: 80
#>     Complete cases: 80
#>   Parameters:
#>     Covariates:            included
#>     Missing data:          fail
#>     Edge storage:          summed across folds
#>     Selection:             pearson / p_value / 0.01
#>     Construction:          separate / no weighting / raw edges
#>     Model:                 linear regression
#>   Use summary() for aggregate correlations and tidy() for correlation tables.
summary(result)
#> CPM summary:
#>   Number of folds: 5
#>   Pooled correlations (Pearson):
#>     Joint: -0.084
#>     Positive: 0.062
#>     Negative: -0.177
#>   Fold-wise correlations (Pearson):
#>     Joint: -0.071 (SE 0.045)
#>     Positive: 0.030 (SE 0.055)
#>     Negative: -0.174 (SE 0.097)
#>   Selected edges:
#>     Positive: 1.00%
#>     Negative: 0.50%

This keeps CPM-specific steps such as covariate handling, edge selection, and model training inside each assessment fold.

Inspect Predictions and Edges

CPM results keep observation-level predictions on the object, while summary() reports pooled and fold-wise out-of-fold correlations.

predictions <- result$predictions

summary_result <- summary(result)

summary_result
#> CPM summary:
#>   Number of folds: 5
#>   Pooled correlations (Pearson):
#>     Joint: -0.084
#>     Positive: 0.062
#>     Negative: -0.177
#>   Fold-wise correlations (Pearson):
#>     Joint: -0.071 (SE 0.045)
#>     Positive: 0.030 (SE 0.055)
#>     Negative: -0.174 (SE 0.097)
#>   Selected edges:
#>     Positive: 1.00%
#>     Negative: 0.50%
head(summary_result[["metrics"]])
#>             level prediction    estimate  std_error  method
#> 1          pooled      joint -0.08438626         NA pearson
#> 2          pooled   positive  0.06200956         NA pearson
#> 3          pooled   negative -0.17727972         NA pearson
#> joint    foldwise      joint -0.07073201 0.04541292 pearson
#> positive foldwise   positive  0.02959662 0.05523617 pearson
#> negative foldwise   negative -0.17395274 0.09676208 pearson
head(predictions)
#>   row fold   observed        joint     positive      negative
#> 1   1    5 -0.6339456  0.344338065  0.344338065  2.602085e-18
#> 2   2    1  0.4116546 -0.478738601  0.028245399 -5.179443e-01
#> 3   3    1  0.2898583 -0.032769603  0.073529511 -1.070810e-01
#> 4   4    3  0.7870086  0.001199379  0.001199379  8.673617e-18
#> 5   5    5  0.1169538 -0.028386998 -0.028386998  2.602085e-18
#> 6   6    3  0.7875511  0.264960292  0.264960292  8.673617e-18
head(tidy(result, component = "metrics"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>    fold n_assess prediction estimate method 
#>   <int>    <int> <chr>         <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1     1       16 joint       -0.0488 pearson
#> 2     1       16 positive    -0.0913 pearson
#> 3     1       16 negative     0.0151 pearson
#> 4     2       16 joint       -0.142  pearson
#> 5     2       16 positive     0.168  pearson
#> 6     2       16 negative    -0.233  pearson
head(tidy(result, component = "metrics", level = "pooled"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   prediction estimate method 
#>   <chr>         <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1 joint       -0.0844 pearson
#> 2 positive     0.0620 pearson
#> 3 negative    -0.177  pearson

These three outputs have slightly different jobs:

  • summary(result) prints the default aggregate report;
  • summary(result)[["metrics"]] exposes the compact summary-level metric table stored on the summary object;
  • tidy(result, component = "metrics") returns the raw fold-wise metric table for further filtering, plotting, or export, while level = "pooled" returns pooled metrics.

By default, cpm() uses return_edges = "sum" and stores fold-aggregated edge selection counts. This makes edge summaries immediately available in the common fold-based workflow.

If you want to control edge storage explicitly:

edge_result <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav,
  spec = spec(),
  covariates = covariates,
  resamples = 5,
  return_edges = "sum"
)

dim(edge_result$edges)
#> [1] 200   2

predictions returns one row per original observation. If na_action = "exclude" removed subjects before fitting, those rows are still present and their fold value is NA.

When return_edges = "sum", cpmr stores fold-summed edge counts for each edge. If memory matters, switch to return_edges = "none" or use return_edges = "all" only when fold-wise edge arrays are truly needed.

Custom Resamples

If you already have a partition scheme, pass it through resamples.

custom_resamples <- split(
  seq_len(n),
  cut(seq_len(n), breaks = 4, labels = FALSE)
)

custom_obj <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav,
  spec = spec(),
  resamples = custom_resamples,
  return_edges = "none"
)

summary(custom_obj)
#> CPM summary:
#>   Number of folds: 4
#>   Pooled correlations (Pearson):
#>     Joint: 0.143
#>     Positive: 0.169
#>     Negative: -0.003
#>   Fold-wise correlations (Pearson):
#>     Joint: 0.154 (SE 0.119)
#>     Positive: 0.240 (SE 0.129)
#>     Negative: 0.031 (SE 0.111)

Custom resamples must:

  • be supplied as assessment-row indices;
  • cover every complete-case subject exactly once;
  • not overlap across folds.

When na_action = "exclude", those indices still refer to original row numbers of the complete-case subjects kept in the analysis.

Missing-Data Handling

Set na_action = "exclude" if you want cpmr to fit on complete cases while preserving original row positions in the outputs.

behav_with_na <- behav
behav_with_na[c(3, 11)] <- NA_real_

na_obj <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav_with_na,
  spec = spec(),
  resamples = 5,
  na_action = "exclude"
)

na_predictions <- na_obj$predictions
na_predictions[na_predictions$row %in% c(3, 11), ]
#>    row fold observed joint positive negative
#> 3    3   NA       NA    NA       NA       NA
#> 11  11   NA       NA    NA       NA       NA

This behavior matters when you need to merge predictions back to subject-level metadata after assessment.

Next Steps

After you are comfortable with the native path:

  • read the leakage-focused article if you need a more detailed covariate handling example;
  • keep a spec() object around when you want an explicit reusable parameter object.
